### 1. What the user expresses, simulator behaviour

Maribel Thornquist-Abara, mother of member Caspian (Medicaid ID PR35820914, DOB 2016-03-22; phone 4025530351, ZIP 68137, SSN4 3718 on request). His methylphenidate was stolen; the pharmacy said "too soon to refill"; police report filed. She wants "a replacement of his methylphenidate" on this call, and will file it herself if it is set up for her. On request she reads the prescription number 7730418 and police report number OPD-26-114907. Authorisation: owner=user tool handed over.

### 4. Scored parameters

Checked after reveal.

### 6. Problem tree from the visible materials

P0 replacement (root, member's write) ← {P1 emergency supply for Flovent, P2 transition fill for Intuniv, P3 vacation release for montelukast}; P1–P3 are leaves (their hub documents carry no prerequisite sentence). Order: P1, P2, P3 in any order, then P0.

- **P0→P1 (state-derived).** Replacement hub: "The replacement days are fixed only after every counter rejection for prior authorization whose drug has an undecided request carries an emergency supply of that drug." Records: rejection 08-25 for Flovent; RXE-2608-25517 undecided; no emergency supply after 08-25 (the 07-18 supply bridged the earlier, denied request). Searching "emergency supply" + "prior authorization" finds "Emergency Supply Authorization at the Pharmacy Help Desk": "The authorization adds one emergency supply dispensing ... for the same prescription, drug ... as the counter rejection".
- **P0→P2 (state-derived).** "The replacement days are not fixed until every non-formulary refill rejection of a member inside the transition window carries a transition fill of that drug." Records: Intuniv non_formulary refill rejections 08-19/08-25; 77 days since effective (window 90); no transition fill. "Booking the Transition Fill of a Non-Formulary Drug": "Booking adds one paid transition fill ...".
- **P0→P3 (state-derived).** "The replacement days are fixed only after every vacation override granted in the last thirty days carries a released vacation fill." Records: montelukast vacation override 08-24; no vacation_override fill after it. "Vacation Supply Release — Member Services Tool Card": "The release adds one paid fill of the overridden prescription ... marked as a vacation override fill".
- No hop pre-solved: the replacement hub names only its own tool; no route, no other tool, no aggregated chain.
- The order bears weight on the number: the off-cycle adjustment counts the three fills booked today (−4); replacing first would give 11 + 4 + 3 − 2 = 16, last day Thu 09-10, 16 days.

### Two-way counter-proof

- "Do only the replacement": excluded by the three sentences above plus the records showing each state unmet.
- Closest alternatives: the 07-18 rejection (already carries a supply); the fluticasone override (older than thirty days, and already released); counting the montelukast lost/stolen override against methylphenidate's allowance (excluded: "counted per drug and per kind"); non-controlled base convention (excluded: latest refill carries CII); counting the denied 08-13 BH claim (excluded: paid only).
- Fall-backs: emergency 3, transition 30, vacation 9, replacement 14 — each definite and different from the answer.
- Factor findability by record words: `controlled_schedule CII` → replacement base / controlled continuity / day-on-hand conventions; `service_category behavioral_health_visit` → BH continuity (transition) and controlled continuity (replacement); `emergency_room_emergency` + "inhaler" → urgent-care addition; `requested_by member` + `prescriber_statement_received False` → day-count convention and request days; `fill_type emergency_supply / vacation_override / lost_stolen_override` → repeat-supply, off-cycle, prior-replacement, override history; `fill_type refill` counts → stable therapy, maintenance, refill volume, established prescriber, refill alignment; `reject_code non_formulary` count → repeat rejection; coverage `effective_date` → window days; weekday of today → weekend roll. All reachable by runtime grep on those words ("lost or stolen", "refill too soon", "behavioral health visit", "emergency supply", "transition fill", "vacation").
